overview: Champa was a collection of Indianized Cham kingdoms that thrived on maritime trade along the Vietnamese coast for over a millennium. Known for spectacular brick temple towers dedicated to Shiva, skilled seafaring and fierce resistance against Vietnamese and Khmer expansion.

items.text: Brick temple towers at My Son sanctuary rival Angkor in architectural sophistication.
Sandstone sculptures of Shiva, Vishnu and apsaras in a distinctive Cham style.
Maritime trade in agarwood, ivory, gold and spices connected China, India and the archipelago.
Cham sailors and merchants active throughout Southeast Asian waters.
Hinduism, particularly Shaivism, practiced alongside Buddhism and indigenous beliefs.
Sanskrit inscriptions record royal genealogies and religious endowments.
My Son Sanctuary is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Cham communities survive in Vietnam and Cambodia, preserving their language and traditions.

fall.text: The last remnants of Champa were fully annexed by the Vietnamese Nguyen dynasty.
